about: The chaos suite's legs (C14 brief, amended 2026-10-20): each harness/cases/<case>.sh, variant and repeat is one leg of chaos.yml. The restart cases run 3 times and run-chaos.sh prints the worst outage. n is the brief's case number. `owed` (C14 fix round 3, item 4) names the docs/_INDEX.md Owed row behind each check a leg is known to fail (a row, or a list tried in order), so run-chaos.sh's table says which reds are explained; it never changes a verdict, and an owed red is as red as any other. A row is named for a failed check only when its `owed_signatures` filter (jq over that leg's verdict.json, its measures the evidence of the row's own cause) holds in that run (fix round 4, the re-review's I-3); else the check reads NOT OWED with the signature absent. A row leaves the map when its fix merges, and a red on its checks then reads NOT OWED: Owed 85 (a restarted container's CEF never starting; PR #54, main 263b08a), Owed 84 (a late sink's backlog; PR #57) and Owed 70 (a) (a fast GPU-death loop counted late; PR #55), all 2026-10-24, main 567cfcc. Owed 87 stays (the PR #65 review's I-2): cases 5 and 12 pass on the sink's own error (the coordinator's decision, 2026-10-24), and case 17, built to witness the stall rule, reds on CI because rtmp2sink's own 5 s socket timeout swaps first there too (its 8 KiB cap does not hold the socket open); the rule's fate is the owner's. Its signature (read from `stall_swap`'s measure) holds only when the sink's own error path held in full and, in case 17 (`queue_past_cap`), the cap was set as asked and the queue still ran past it, so any other red on those checks reads NOT OWED; in cases 5 and 12 an error path held in full passes the check, so a red there never holds it. Cases 4, 5 and 12 each run twice, once per phase of the clear (no variant: a connect pending; `backoff`: after one failed; the re-review's I-5).

owed_signatures.87: .measures.stall_swap.reason == "error" and .measures.stall_swap.error_path_passes == true and (.measures.stall_swap | if has("queue_past_cap") then .queue_past_cap == true else true end)

owed_titles.86: the ladder never moves under CPU starvation, and the beats read healthy
owed_titles.87: the stall rule never beats rtmp2sink's own 5 s socket timeout (the same gap, timed from the same write): a stalled destination is swapped by the sink's error, and case 17's 8 KiB cap does not hold the socket open
